title: ISO/IEC 27001 Alignment (Draft One-Pager) — Redwood Inference
content:
Redwood Inference — ISO/IEC 27001 Alignment (Draft, customer-facing one-pager)
Last updated: 2026-02-14
Owner: GRC (Olga Petrov) | Reviews: Security Eng (Marcus Lin), Product Security (Naomi Feldman), Legal (Michael Grant)

1) Purpose
This one-pager helps Sales/SE teams answer ISO 27001-related questions accurately and consistently without implying certification. It summarizes how Redwood’s security program and control environment align to common ISO/IEC 27001 expectations and Annex A control themes.

2) The most important rule (do not misrepresent)
Redwood should not state or imply that we are “ISO 27001 certified,” “ISO compliant,” or “ISO audited,” unless GRC has confirmed we hold an active ISO/IEC 27001 certificate covering the relevant scope.

Approved positioning is “alignment” and “control mapping,” anchored by verifiable audit evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report under NDA).

3) Copy-ready approved language (use in RFPs / questionnaires)
A) Short answer
“Redwood Inference maintains a mature information security program designed around industry-standard security control objectives. While Redwood is not currently ISO/IEC 27001 certified, many of our policies, procedures, and technical controls align with ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27002 control themes. We can provide our SOC 2 report and supporting security documentation under NDA upon request.”

B) When asked: “Are you ISO 27001 certified?”
“Not at this time. Redwood can share third-party assurance materials (e.g., SOC 2 report) under NDA and discuss how our security program maps to ISO 27001 control expectations.”

C) When asked: “Do you have an ISMS?”
“Redwood maintains an internal security management program with documented policies, risk management processes, access control standards, incident response procedures, vendor risk practices, and security training. We can share high-level summaries and evidence of operation under NDA.”

4) What not to say (examples)
- “We are ISO 27001 compliant.” (ISO 27001 is a certifiable management system standard; ‘compliant’ is commonly interpreted as certified.)
- “ISO 27001 audited.” (Unless specifically audited/certified for ISO.)
- “Meets all ISO 27001 controls.” (ISO scope and applicability vary; avoid absolutes.)
- “Covers any customer environment.” (Hosted/Dedicated/Private differ; use shared responsibility language.)

5) Scope and shared responsibility (must be included for accuracy)
Redwood offers multiple deployment modes; control responsibility boundaries differ.
- Hosted API: Redwood operates the full platform service (infrastructure, runtime, control plane) and provides customer-facing security controls (SSO/RBAC, audit logs, retention options, etc.).
- Dedicated: Redwood operates dedicated capacity with additional isolation; customer configuration and operational responsibilities are documented.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Responsibility is shared; Redwood provides the software/control plane components as contracted, while the customer manages portions of network, identity, host hardening, and physical security (especially for on-prem).

Use this line when needed:
“Security responsibilities vary by deployment model. Redwood provides platform controls and documentation; customers manage their own user access governance, endpoint/device security, and (in Private/on-prem) certain infrastructure and physical controls.”

6) ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A theme mapping (high level)
Note: This is a theme-to-control mapping for customer understanding; it is not a statement of certification.

6.1 Organizational controls (policies, governance, risk)
- Security governance & policy framework
  • Redwood maintains documented security policies and standards (access control, encryption, vulnerability management, incident response, vendor management).
  • Evidence: policy excerpts/summaries available under NDA via GRC.
- Risk management
  • Redwood performs periodic risk assessments and tracks remediation through internal ownership and change control.
  • Evidence: risk process summary; selected artifacts under NDA.
- Supplier & subprocessor management
  • Third-party due diligence and contract controls are applied for subprocessors.
  • Evidence: subprocessor list and vendor security posture documentation provided via the evidence request process.

6.2 People controls (training, access lifecycle)
- Security awareness training
  • Security training is required for employees; access is role-based.
  • Evidence: training program attestation under NDA.
- Joiner/mover/leaver controls
  • Access provisioning and deprovisioning follow documented processes; privileged access is restricted.
  • Product capability: RBAC roles and permissions for Console/API; SSO (SAML) for supported plans.

6.3 Physical controls
- Data center physical security
  • In Hosted/Dedicated, underlying cloud data centers provide physical security controls; Redwood relies on cloud provider attestations.
  • In on-prem Private deployments, physical security is primarily customer-managed.

6.4 Technological controls (identity, crypto, logging, SDLC)
- Identity & access management
  • SSO/SAML support (where enabled), RBAC, and least-privilege practices.
  • Administrative access to production is restricted and monitored.
- Cryptography (in transit / at rest)
  • Encryption in transit via TLS; encryption at rest for supported storage layers.
  • Key management options vary by deployment mode; for Private/VPC, customer-managed key integrations may be available by contract.
- Logging & monitoring
  • Audit logging for key administrative and security-relevant events; export options may be supported for enterprise deployments.
  • Retention controls vary; confirm customer requirements and reference the retention one-pager.
- Secure development lifecycle
  • Security reviews, vulnerability management, and patching practices are in place.
  • Evidence: SOC 2 control descriptions, vulnerability management summary under NDA.
- Incident management
  • Documented incident response process with defined escalation and communication pathways.
  • Evidence: IR policy summary under NDA.
- Business continuity
  • Service resilience practices exist; exact commitments depend on plan and deployment.

7) Suggested questionnaire guidance (how to translate ISO questions into Redwood answers)
- If a questionnaire expects “ISO certificate number,” respond with: “Not currently ISO certified; can provide SOC 2 report under NDA.”
- If a question references “Statement of Applicability (SoA),” respond with: “Not applicable (no ISO 27001 certification/SoA). We can provide a control mapping summary and assurance reports under NDA.”
- If a question asks for “Annex A control implementation,” respond with the theme mapping above plus deployment-mode caveats.

8) Evidence and where to route requests
- SOC 2 report and restricted evidence: available under NDA via the formal evidence request process.
- Routing: Ask the customer to sign NDA (if required) and submit an evidence request per the SOC 2 / Evidence Request Playbook.
Internal note: Do not email restricted artifacts directly to customers from personal inboxes. Use the approved process and record the request.

9) Internal review / approvals required before sending custom language
Any non-standard claims must be reviewed by:
- GRC (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter) for compliance wording
- Security Engineering (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei) for technical accuracy
- Legal (Michael Grant) if language touches contractual commitments (breach notification timelines, SLAs, audit rights)

10) Open items (for this draft)
- Confirm whether we want to explicitly reference ISO/IEC 27002:2022 (guidance standard) in customer-facing text or keep at ISO 27001 only.
- Align final wording with the updated Security FAQ “What we do and don’t say” section.
- Ensure deployment-mode-specific statements match the latest product docs (SSO/SCIM/RBAC, audit log export, retention controls).

Contact for questions: GRC (Olga Petrov) | Security reviewer: Marcus Lin | Product Security PM: Naomi Feldman
